key_insight: Computational analysis identified three psoriatic arthritis synovial pathotypes—Dense Myeloid, Fibro-Stromal, and Angio-Lymphoid—rather than cancer drug discovery targets.
clinical_relevance: These tissue patterns could support future treatment stratification in psoriatic arthritis, but their predictive utility remains unvalidated.
method: Ultrasound-guided synovial biopsies from 61 patients, including 22 with psoriatic arthritis.
Multi-modal staining and automated whole-slide image analysis quantified immune, vascular, and stromal features.
Unsupervised hierarchical clustering identified pathotypes and explored clinical and treatment-response associations.
evidence_signal: In the 22-patient psoriatic arthritis cohort, reported treatment-response rates were 44% for Fibro-Stromal, 50% for Dense Myeloid, and 80% for Angio-Lymphoid, described as a trend rather than a validated predictive effect.
watch_item: The small discovery cohort requires independent prospective validation before pathotypes or the proposed four-marker decision tree can guide treatment.
paper_title: Redefining Synovial Pathotypes in Psoriatic Arthritis through Multi-Modal Histology and Machine Learning (The PSYNOVIUM Study)
